prompt:
Two reports turned out to be the same incident. A customer's receiving endpoint got every "issue created" and "status changed" webhook two or three times. At the same moments the audit log started recording each action more than once, and the workspace's issues-used counter began climbing by two or three per new issue. Ops confirmed that it starts right after the server re-wires its event handlers: the dev hot reload does this, and so does the "restart background workers" button in the ops console. Both detach the handlers and then attach them again. A freshly started process behaves correctly. Oddly, in-app notifications (for example "You were assigned an issue") were never duplicated.

After your fix, and after any number of detach and re-attach cycles, each action must produce exactly one webhook delivery per subscribed endpoint, one audit-log row and one usage increment. While the handlers are detached, none of those may be produced. Registering again without detaching first must stay a no-op. In-app notifications must keep being delivered exactly once throughout, including while the other handlers are detached.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Injected (single root cause, shared lib): the in-process event bus's subscribe() was made copy-on-write (a new Set per subscribe, installed in the map) but its unsubscribe closure still deletes from the Set captured at subscribe time. Once any later subscribe to the same event type has replaced the Set, that unsubscribe is a silent no-op. The event registry attaches four listener groups (activity, search, usage, webhooks) to the same types in sequence, so unregisterEventHandlers() leaves most of them attached and a re-register doubles them. Symptoms surface in webhook-service, activity-service and usage-service; the registry and its detach logic look correct; the cause is in src/lib. The notification fan-out subscribes once at module load and is never detached, which is why notifications stay single. Edge cases: the fix must not reset the whole bus on unregister (that kills the notification fan-out, which is checked), and detaching must actually stop the handlers (checked while detached). The hidden test also pins the bus contract directly (unsubscribing handlers 1 and 3 of 3 leaves only handler 2). No visible test exercises detach after a later subscribe, so the visible suite stays green. Validation: bug -> tsc 0, visible 617/617; hidden 4/4 fail; bug+solution -> hidden 4/4, full 621/621, tsc 0; naive (resetEventBus in unregister) -> 4/4 fail (notifications lost); naive2 (never re-attach after first registration) -> 4/4 fail; hidden x3 stable.
